conclusion: The pinned G public Model2 authoring path forces ingress.default=allow and then adds PNCS to the final PSEC capability list. Removing caller PNCS or relaxing only native07's agentic-only GO gate cannot produce the proposed no-PNCS PSEC proxy request. A separate native-spec adapter would be a new, currently unverified policy experiment, not a small supported G configuration change.

facts: allowedProxyPeer without runtime networkProxy is rejected.
Runtime proxy requires an ingress policy whose default is allow.
Identity-scoped proxy requires hostLoopback=deny; reserved MXC-Loopback cannot be provided as caller peer.
Directional networking always uses capability gates; legacy enforcementMode does not disable them.
When directional policy exists, caller internetClient, internetClientServer, PNCS and networkLoopback entries are removed before policy mapping.
ingress.default=allow then ensures privateNetworkClientServer is present.
The PSEC builder calls effective_capabilities, which invokes add_default_network_capabilities.
The final capability names are serialized into the PSEC capabilities field.
Proxy policy and direct egress policy use mutually exclusive authoring branches.
A proxy policy omits the native ingress table and carries allowed_appcontainer_peer separately.
The native schema has an optional capabilities string and network proxy/egress/allowed_appcontainer_peer/ingress fields.
The schema does not contain a DNS switch or an LPAC switch.
An optional native capabilities field is not evidence that proxy access without PNCS works.
Model2 explicitly lists PNCS as the client capability selected through ingress.allow.
The private-network mapping describes capability as a prerequisite; peer identity adds binding rather than replacing capability.

The host-loopback discussion says a peer alone can create an environment while its client cannot reach the host proxy. This is upstream documentation, not a fresh measurement of the exact proposed Agentic-only identity-scoped tuple on this host.

current_native_gate.observation: native07 accepts agentic-only for identity READY and Finish but rejects every network GO before socket/DNS initialization.

policy_facts: Preferred variant sets egress default deny with one exact loopback TCP allow, ingress default deny, hostLoopback deny.
It does not set runtime networkProxy or allowedProxyPeer.
The source-bound diagnostic patch requires empty caller capabilities and removes automatically added internetClient only for the exact matching non-proxy policy.
The archived source projection labels the resulting capabilities field null; this is not a published full held-token capability enumeration. No PNCS is requested by that preferred policy.
observation_facts: The preferred DNS groups had complete positive controls/capture and reported no contained nonce queries.
The reported parent/child returns were getaddrinfo11001 and DNS A/AAAA5.
Proxy transport roundtrips remained zero and internal TCP probes reported10013.
The result was diagnostic-only and failed product acceptance; kernel PSEC contract version was not confirmed.
limitations: This supports retaining the finite historical negative result under its own policy and source.
It does not establish current Model2 no-PNCS proxy connectivity, current DnsQueryEx standard53 behavior, or an exact Agentic-only held token on today's cell.
No historical absence or API5 is used as a repair or Linux-equivalence claim.

learn_example.observation: The example passes Capabilities/NumberOfCapabilities to CreateAppContainerProfile and reuses them in SECURITY_CAPABILITIES for launch.

api_contracts.observation: Capabilities are described as requested UWP capabilities if applicable; no requirement that all future process tokens exactly equal this profile-creation list is stated.
The structure specifies the process AppContainer SID and capabilities; no profile-list equality requirement is stated.

facts: The pinned G AppContainer runner calls CreateAppContainerProfile with None, corresponding to an empty capability slice.
It separately supplies the resolved capability SID_AND_ATTRIBUTES at process construction and adds OPT_OUT for least-privilege mode.
Thus the same general empty-profile/nonempty-process pattern already exists in the pinned upstream implementation. This is source evidence, not proof of this host's failing invocation.

profile_capability_authoring_review.conclusion: The Learn example's matching lists do not prove the current profile list is erroneous. Given the pinned G pattern, changing profile capabilities is not presently an evidence-backed root-cause repair.
